key_insight: A Fourier neural operator learns a numerically computed family of nonlinear standing waves, predicting free-surface geometry, velocity potential and surface dipole density.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate offers a route to efficient repeated evaluation of idealized free-surface waves across a parameterized family.
method: Train on a one-parameter family of symmetric standing waves in infinitely deep, inviscid, irrotational flow.
Map an initial wave profile at rest and normalized observation time to three surface fields.
Evaluate extrapolation toward free-fall and linear limits, alongside an independent governing-equation residual.
evidence_signal: In-distribution tests show uniformly small relative errors; extrapolation errors localize near sharpening crests toward free fall, while relative errors grow as amplitudes vanish toward the linear limit.
watch_item: Validation is limited to one standing-wave family, and FNO spectral truncation can hinder resolution of sharp crests.
paper_title: Learning the solution operator of standing waves with a Fourier neural operator
